events.summaryEn: The Buddhist temple Hōryūji is established in the Asuka region. The Met describes the compound as Japan's earliest extant Buddhist temple, containing the world's oldest surviving wooden structure.
events.selectionNote: The source calls it Japan's earliest extant Buddhist temple.

events.titleEn: Li Yuan founds the Tang dynasty
events.summaryEn: Li Yuan, from a northern aristocratic family with a long record of government service, seizes the throne, restores order and founds the Tang dynasty, ruling as Emperor Gaozu until 626.
events.selectionNote: The founding of the Tang dynasty.

events.titleEn: A ship burial is laid at Sutton Hoo
events.summaryEn: A ship burial is laid under a mound at Sutton Hoo, with grave goods inside a wooden ship: an iron helmet with tinned bronze foil, gold buckles inlaid with niello and a purse cover with cloisonné enamel. No body has been found, perhaps because of the acid soil, and coins among the goods help date the burial.
events.selectionNote: A dated elite ship burial in early Anglo-Saxon England.

events.summaryEn: The pilgrim Xuanzang travels to India and Southeast Asia. His translations spur the growth of Buddhism in China, and his travel account, Records of the Western Regions, remains a key source for South Asian history.
events.selectionNote: A pilgrimage whose translations and travel account the source credits with spurring Chinese Buddhism and documenting South Asian history.

events.summaryEn: Arab Muslim armies conquer Egypt during the caliphate of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab. They found al-Fustat, the garrison town that later becomes part of Cairo, and build Egypt's first congregational mosque for the army.
events.selectionNote: Egypt comes under Muslim rule and gains its first congregational mosque.

date.noteEn: The Met's entry spans 634–644, the reign of 'Umar, and dates the battle itself to 642.

events.titleEn: Arab armies defeat the Sasanians at Nahavand
events.summaryEn: Arab Muslim armies defeat Sasanian forces at the battle of Nahavand, the de facto end of the Sasanian empire. The last Sasanian ruler, Yazdgard III, flees to Merv, where he dies in 651.
events.selectionNote: The battle that the source calls the de facto end of the Sasanian empire.

events.titleEn: Emperor Kōtoku issues the Taika Reform
events.summaryEn: Emperor Kōtoku issues the Taika Reform to strengthen imperial authority and weaken the aristocratic families. On the Chinese model, all farmland becomes the emperor's property and all inhabitants his subjects, governed by a merit-based bureaucracy.
events.selectionNote: Centralises land and government in Japan on the Chinese model.

date.noteEn: The Met dates the burning to about 650 and calls the cause a possible internal crisis.

events.summaryEn: The main temples and elite residences of central Teotihuacan are burned and carved cult objects smashed, perhaps in an internal political and economic crisis. Many apartment compounds are abandoned, though parts of the city remain inhabited until about 900.
events.selectionNote: Marks the collapse of central Teotihuacan; the status marks the uncertain cause.

events.titleEn: The Synod of Whitby chooses Roman practice
events.summaryEn: The Synod of Whitby meets to settle liturgical conflicts between the Celtic and Roman branches of Christianity in England. It decides to follow the Roman church, which draws England closer to Rome and continental Europe.
events.selectionNote: Settles the English church's alignment with Rome.

events.summaryEn: The Tang–Silla allies, after eight years consolidating their hold on former Baekje lands, invade Goguryeo. Weakened by earlier Sui and Tang assaults and by internal dissension, the northern kingdom falls quickly.
events.selectionNote: Ends the northern Korean kingdom of Goguryeo.

date.noteEn: The Met places the campaign and the founding of Kairouan under 670 without separating their years.

events.titleEn: 'Uqba ibn Nafi' conquers the Maghrib and founds Kairouan
events.summaryEn: Muslim armies under 'Uqba ibn Nafi' fight Berber groups and conquer the land from northern Tunisia to Tangier, establishing Umayyad rule in North Africa. 'Uqba founds the city of Kairouan.
events.selectionNote: Establishes Umayyad rule in North Africa and founds Kairouan.

events.titleEn: Silla drives out the Tang and unifies Korea
events.summaryEn: Silla-led resistance forces Tang troops to withdraw into Manchuria. For the first time almost the whole Korean peninsula, all but a narrow band in the north, comes under one Korean government, Unified Silla.
events.selectionNote: The source calls it the first time nearly the whole peninsula came under one Korean government.

events.titleEn: A former Goguryeo general founds Barhae
events.summaryEn: A former Goguryeo general founds the kingdom of Barhae (Chinese: Bohai), which holds most of Goguryeo's former lands in Manchuria. Barhae and Unified Silla avoid war until the Khitan destroy Barhae in 926.
events.selectionNote: The successor kingdom to Goguryeo in Manchuria.
